## 2

I understand why you might be skeptical, especially when misinformation can look convincing online. However, the evidence for a round Earth comes from many independent sources: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, different stars being visible at different latitudes, time zones, lunar eclipses, satellite communication, and direct observations from space by many countries and private companies. These observations all fit a roughly spherical Earth far better than a flat one. It’s reasonable to ask how we know something, but the explanations should account for all the evidence, not just a few suspicious-looking photos.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light fills the sky above us.

Why isn’t the sky violet, if violet scatters even more? Our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and sunlight contains less violet. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more reds and oranges to reach our eyes.
